title: Where Bandwidth Control sits in policy enforcement
aliases: does blocked traffic reach bandwidth control

checks.do: Whether the transaction was blocked or allowed by the earlier stages, since only transactions that every earlier stage allowed reach Bandwidth Control.
Which rules shape the transaction, only once it is known that it was allowed.

block-stops-later-policies.statement: In the web module a transaction that violates a policy is blocked immediately and the policies that follow are not enforced.

quotes: the Public Service Edge immediately blocks that transaction and does not continue enforcing the policies that follow.

last-in-web-order.statement: Bandwidth Control is the final entry in the ordered policy lists the web module applies to HTTP GET and POST requests, to responses, and to the domain-only pass on CONNECT or SNI.
last-in-web-order.conditions: Read from the capture: Bandwidth Control is the last item in each of the four ordered lists. No sentence says in words that it is last.

quotes: Bandwidth Control: The Public Service Edge checks if the request is allowed full or reduced bandwidth
evidence.after: This is a user request to retrieve a resource from the web (e.g., a web page).

quotes: Bandwidth Control: The Public Service Edge checks how much bandwidth to allocate the request

usage-decides.statement: Bandwidth Control decides whether a request gets full or reduced bandwidth from the organization's Bandwidth Control policy and the current bandwidth usage at the user's location.

quotes: based on your organization's Bandwidth Control policy and the current bandwidth usage at the user
evidence.after: This is a user request to retrieve a resource from the web (e.g., a web page).

only-surviving-traffic.statement: Traffic blocked by the Firewall module or by an earlier web policy never reaches Bandwidth Control, so Bandwidth Control only shapes transactions that every earlier stage allowed.
only-surviving-traffic.conditions: Derived from the firewall-first rule, the immediate-block rule and Bandwidth Control's position at the end of the lists.
